messages:
Lexi: quick sketch — extraction idea: per-tenant KMS sidecar. small process co-located with tenant runtime that holds wrapped keys, performs unwrap/sign operations, and emits signed audit events. goal: shrink central KMS blast radius and make HSM plugin management for private deployments simpler.

Omar: sounds promising. main concern: extra network hop on every sign/unseal? how much latency are we adding? :thinking_face:

Lexi: plan is envelope encryption + in-memory ephemeral key cache. sidecar stores only wrapped keys, unwraps once on first use, keeps ephemeral key for a short TTL (e.g., 30s). expected p99 extra latency for hot keys ~1-3ms. cold unwraps will be slower but rare.

Nina: memory residency is a risk. we need mprotect/no-swap, clear-on-free, and strict rotation. threat model: if sidecar is compromised on host what do we lose?

Chris: ops viewpoint — sidecar reduces single-point blast radius but increases service count and operational surface. require attestation and control-plane RBAC so sidecar only accepts signed policy from control. sidecar itself should not be a policy authority.

Lexi: agreed. proposed defenses: 1) mTLS + node identity for sidecar API, 2) OS memory protections + scrub on eviction, 3) HSM-only mode (sidecar never holds plaintext keys; unwrap and operations happen inside HSM).

Omar: migration question: how to migrate tenants without downtime? we cant just flip everyone.

Lexi: feature-flag per-tenant + proxy fallback. flow: default path remains central KMS. enable sidecar for canary tenants (small cohort). sidecar proxies to central KMS if it cannot unwrap or HSM is unavailable. rollback: flip flag back to central.

Nina: audit stream MUST be tamper-evident. sidecar should sign audit entries and stream to central immutable store, or for private installs push to customers audit collector. include sequence numbers and upload acknowledgements.

Chris: monitoring: unwrap latency histogram, cache hit ratio, in-memory residency metric, auth failures. define SLOs for unwrap latency and sidecar availability. create alerting on high unwrap error rates and falling acked-audit rate.

auditor-bot: note — compliance checklist: document key rotation, attestation records, and HSM integration tests. filed INF-8254 for followup.

Omar: one more: backups and restore semantics for private/onprem customers?

Lexi: wrapped keys are backup-safe. operator must manage HSM master credentials. plaintext keys must never be backed up. include an upgrade tool to rewrap keys if master KMS changes.

Nina: RFC must call out exact crypto primitives: AES-GCM for envelope + HKDF derivation, key wrapping via RSA-OAEP or KMS-provider wrap APIs. no bespoke crypto.

Chris: ops runbook items: 1) feature-flag flipback steps, 2) circuit breaker when unwrap error-rate > threshold, 3) automatic proxy-to-central when >X errors, 4) emergency rotate & revoke flow documented.

Lexi: short rollout checklist: implement sidecar with wrapped-key store + cache; add mTLS and node attestation; sign & stream audit records; feature-flag gating + proxy fallback; canary on 3 non-critical tenants for 2 weeks; monitor unwrap latency, cache hit, and audit delivery; iterate and expand.

Omar: add mem/cpu overhead numbers per sidecar for capacity planning.

Nina: run a SecEng tabletop on the threat model before canary.

Lexi: will draft RFC with diagrams, sample configs, perf targets, and rollback checklist. ping me to review. :thumbsup:
